AmbienceTrack.description:
Server-allowlisted ambience bed the client may request on its OUTPUT audio.

A NAME, never a filesystem path: the server resolves it to a synthesized
looping bed. Adding a bed is one entry here — the resolver derives its
allowlist from this enum.
AmbienceTrack.title: AmbienceTrack

ExternalRealtimeDialBody.description: Request body for placing an outbound dial on a running session.

caller_number.description: E.164 caller-ID to present, e.g. +14155550100. Must be an ACTIVE number in the workspace's pool (rejected with 400 caller_number_not_available otherwise). Omit to use the trunk default.
caller_number.title: Caller Number

ExternalRealtimeDialBody.title: ExternalRealtimeDialBody

ExternalRealtimeDialResponse.description:
Result of ``POST /session/{id}/dial`` — the dial was queued. The
call rings asynchronously; ``dial_id`` is the handle to correlate it.
Live status / outcome is observed via session events, not this response.
ExternalRealtimeDialResponse.title: ExternalRealtimeDialResponse

external_user_id.description: Opaque developer-supplied identifier for the end user — letters, digits, dot, underscore, plus, at-sign, or hyphen (emails work), up to 128 chars. The same value binds to the same auto-provisioned project on repeat calls.
external_user_id.title: External User Id

RealtimeAmbienceConfig.description:
Background-ambience bed mixed into the assistant's OUTPUT audio
(server-side allowlist; additionally gated by the ops flag). Presence of
this object enables the bed; omit it for none. Makes a telephony call
sound like it comes from a staffed room.
RealtimeAmbienceConfig.title: RealtimeAmbienceConfig

RealtimeAudioConfig.description: The agent's audio pipeline, configured once — not per run.
RealtimeAudioConfig.title: RealtimeAudioConfig

RealtimeBotLlmStarted.description:
Model began generating its turn (first text or audio event arrived).

Distinct from ``bot-started-speaking`` so UI can show "thinking…" before
audio is on the wire — useful when the model takes a moment to start
generating, or when tool calls precede speech.
RealtimeBotLlmStarted.title: RealtimeBotLlmStarted

RealtimeBotStartedSpeaking.description:
First audio frame of an assistant turn left the server.

Information-only — UI uses this for "speaking…" indicators / waveform
activation. Clients must NOT gate the mic on this event.
RealtimeBotStartedSpeaking.title: RealtimeBotStartedSpeaking

RealtimeBotTtsStarted.description:
Assistant TTS audio frames started flowing. With a fused-model
upstream this fires close to ``bot-started-speaking``; with separate
STT/LLM/TTS pipelines the gap is larger.
RealtimeBotTtsStarted.title: RealtimeBotTtsStarted

RealtimeCatalogAgentConfig.description:
Run a workspace catalog agent by handle — the stored config runs
verbatim. Only per-run ride-alongs may accompany the launch:
``inputs`` (per-run input values), ``tools`` (client-executed
declarations the server cannot provide), and ``voice`` (per-run
speaking style plus the one cosmetic override). Other stored-config
fields (``instructions``, ``model``, …) are structurally absent from
this variant — sending one is a schema error (``extra="forbid"``), not
a runtime rejection.
RealtimeCatalogAgentConfig.title: RealtimeCatalogAgentConfig

RealtimeCatalogToolSpec.description:
Attach a workspace-defined tool by its catalog name
(``voice_agent_tools.name``); the server resolves the stored definition.

Protocol reservation only: the wire shape is fixed, but neither
session-start flow executes catalog tools yet — a config carrying one is
rejected with a typed 422 (``invalid_tool_config``). Unknown fields are
a schema error.
RealtimeCatalogToolSpec.title: RealtimeCatalogToolSpec

RealtimeClientActivityEnd.description:
Client signals end-of-turn for manual-VAD turn-taking. Distinct from
``RealtimeClientEnd`` (whole-session teardown).
RealtimeClientActivityEnd.title: RealtimeClientActivityEnd

RealtimeClientBindInput.description:
Bind the agent's audio input to this client.

Sent after the client publishes its own audio (the human voice) so the
agent listens to *this* participant. The server binds to the sender's
participant identity — a client can only bind its own input — and the pin is
sticky thereafter. A client that joins only to receive events or serve
client tools, publishing no audio, never sends this and so is never the
voice.
RealtimeClientBindInput.title: RealtimeClientBindInput

RealtimeClientContext.description:
Add text to the model's context without asking it to reply.

The content rides the provider's pre-turn channel, so the model is never
asked for a response and cannot open a turn for it; it reads the note as
background when it next answers the user. This is the opposite of
``send-text``, which *is* a turn.

For live application state (scroll position, selection, current record,
form values) that should inform the agent without interrupting it.
RealtimeClientContext.title: RealtimeClientContext

RealtimeClientEnd.description: User ended the session. Server tears down the upstream session and closes.
RealtimeClientEnd.title: RealtimeClientEnd

RealtimeClientEnvelope.description:
Generic chunked carrier for any oversized client message.

The SDK auto-wraps any outbound message whose JSON exceeds the
transport's per-packet threshold into a sequence of envelope chunks; the
server buffers by ``envelope_id``, concatenates the base64-encoded UTF-8
bytes back into the original JSON, and re-runs classification.

``data`` is a base64-encoded fragment of the UTF-8 bytes of the inner
message JSON. Base64 keeps every chunk ASCII-safe — splitting at byte
boundaries can land mid-codepoint in a raw UTF-8 substring, which would
corrupt the decode on the server.

Ordering is guaranteed by the reliable channel (chunks arrive in ``seq``
order); ``envelope_id`` keeps concurrent envelopes from interleaving.
``seq`` runs ``0..total-1`` and the assembler emits the reassembled
inner message as soon as the last chunk arrives.
RealtimeClientEnvelope.title: RealtimeClientEnvelope

RealtimeClientImage.description:
One image frame from the client — screen share, camera capture, or
any other visual input the application wants to feed to the model.

Carried as base64 in JSON so it rides the same control channel as text
and tool calls (the audio channel stays pure PCM). Oversized frames are
wrapped in ``RealtimeClientEnvelope`` chunks transparently by the SDK.

``stream_id`` lets the application label multiple concurrent video
streams (e.g. ``camera``, ``screen_share_main``).
RealtimeClientImage.title: RealtimeClientImage

RealtimeClientMute.description: Toggle the mic gate. While muted the client drops outbound audio frames.
RealtimeClientMute.title: RealtimeClientMute

RealtimeClientText.description: Send a text message instead of audio.
RealtimeClientText.title: RealtimeClientText

RealtimeClientToolSpec.description:
One client-executed tool, self-described at session start.

The server materializes a session-scoped tool definition from each spec,
so a new client tool ships with a client release alone — no per-tool
backend code. Field names mirror MCP's ``Tool`` descriptor.

Only size/resource bounds are enforced here (they bind at the API edge);
content checks soft-reject per spec server-side and are echoed on
``RealtimeReady.rejected_tools`` — a client can see *why* a spec was
dropped instead of debugging silence.
RealtimeClientToolSpec.title: RealtimeClientToolSpec

RealtimeCosmoCursorPoint.description:
Cursor position for a cosmo turn-context — screen coordinates, AppKit
bottom-left origin.
RealtimeCosmoCursorPoint.title: RealtimeCosmoCursorPoint

RealtimeCosmoSessionState.description:
First-party cosmo event: live session state after a ``set_state`` tool
write — feeds the playground inspector / disposition panel. Carries the
full canonical state, not a delta; ``stage`` is hoisted from
``state["stage"]`` and ``warnings`` are the advisory schema findings the
model also saw in its tool result.
RealtimeCosmoSessionState.title: RealtimeCosmoSessionState

RealtimeCosmoTurnContext.description:
First-party cosmo client message: per-turn desktop context attached to a
user turn. Wire-compatible with the internal ``turn-context`` — the boundary
parses inbound client messages directly against the internal union, so the
``type`` and field names mirror it exactly. Part of the cosmo.* surface.
RealtimeCosmoTurnContext.title: RealtimeCosmoTurnContext

RealtimeCosmoUsage.description:
First-party cosmo event: cumulative token usage for the live session,
split by direction and modality. Emitted for any external session whose
upstream reports usage — translation is stateless, not gated on the
``cosmo`` config block.
RealtimeCosmoUsage.title: RealtimeCosmoUsage

RealtimeCredentialKind.description: Which of the two realtime credentials the server saw.
RealtimeCredentialKind.title: RealtimeCredentialKind

RealtimeDetectObjectsToolSpec.description:
Opt-in to the server-executed object locator, which returns boxes.

Locates a named object in the freshest camera/screen frame — one box
per matching instance — and hands the candidates to the model, which
picks one and passes it to whichever renderer the client declared.
Zero-config; unknown fields are a schema error. Availability is checked
at session start: a deployment that cannot run the tool starts the
session without it and reports the drop on ``ready.rejected_tools``.
A session with no frame gets the tool's own typed answer at call time.
RealtimeDetectObjectsToolSpec.title: RealtimeDetectObjectsToolSpec

RealtimeEndCall.description: End-call action for a server hook (execution lands with #8344).
RealtimeEndCall.title: RealtimeEndCall

RealtimeError.description:
Recoverable or terminal error. Clients switch on ``code`` for
recovery UX.

``fatal=True`` signals the session is dead; the client should tear down
and reconnect rather than retry the current turn. ``fatal=False`` means
this turn failed but the session can continue.
RealtimeError.title: RealtimeError

RealtimeErrorBody.description:
The error payload every non-2xx external API response carries.

``type`` is the error family (``api_error`` / ``validation_error`` /
``internal_error``). ``code`` is the machine-readable rejection code for
typed session-start rejections (e.g. ``version_mismatch``,
``invalid_tool_config``); absent otherwise. ``errors`` lists field-level
violations for ``validation_error`` responses.
RealtimeErrorBody.title: RealtimeErrorBody

RealtimeErrorCode.description: Stable error codes the FE switches on to choose a recovery UX.
RealtimeErrorCode.title: RealtimeErrorCode

RealtimeErrorEnvelope.description: Wire shape of every non-2xx external API response.
RealtimeErrorEnvelope.title: RealtimeErrorEnvelope

RealtimeExamineImageToolSpec.description:
Opt-in to the server-executed frame-examination tool.

Reads the freshest frame of the client's published video (camera or
screen share) at full resolution to answer a fine-detail question.
The server owns the model-facing declaration — zero-config; unknown
fields are a schema error. Sessions without a fresh frame get the
tool's own typed "no frame" answer at call time; there is no
session-start availability gate.
RealtimeExamineImageToolSpec.title: RealtimeExamineImageToolSpec

RealtimeExperimentalParams.description:
Unstable session-config knobs.

Fields here are experimental: they may change shape or disappear without
an ``EXTERNAL_PROTOCOL_VERSION`` bump. Stable equivalents graduate to
top-level ``RealtimeSessionConfig`` fields.
RealtimeExperimentalParams.title: RealtimeExperimentalParams

RealtimeFieldError.description:
One field-level violation from request-schema validation: a path into
the caller's own request plus the standard validation error type and
message. Payload values are never echoed back.
RealtimeFieldError.title: RealtimeFieldError

RealtimeGeminiModelOptions.description:
Gemini-realtime model knobs. Valid only when the selected ``model`` runs
on Gemini; the ``provider`` discriminator makes setting these for any other
provider a schema error rather than a silent no-op.
RealtimeGeminiModelOptions.title: RealtimeGeminiModelOptions

RealtimeInlineAgentConfig.description:
Define the agent inline — the persona/configuration of the model on
the other end, independent of any one run. Reused unchanged across
sessions. Catalog-only fields (``name``, ``inputs``) are structurally
absent — sending one is a schema error (``extra="forbid"``), so a
mistagged catalog launch fails loudly instead of silently running the
neutral default agent.
RealtimeInlineAgentConfig.title: RealtimeInlineAgentConfig

RealtimeModelText.description:
Streaming text-channel fragment from the model.

Distinct from ``transcript``: this is text the model emits alongside its
audio output, not a transcription of the audio itself. In audio sessions
the upstream may write function-call narration here that the model did
NOT speak; in text-only sessions it carries the model's response.
Consumers building a "what was spoken" transcript should subscribe to
``RealtimeTranscriptDelta`` instead.
RealtimeModelText.title: RealtimeModelText

RealtimeOpenAIModelOptions.description:
OpenAI-Realtime model knobs. OpenAI Realtime pins its own sampling and
token limits, so nothing is tunable here today; the block exists so an
OpenAI agent is representable and future knobs have a typed home.
RealtimeOpenAIModelOptions.title: RealtimeOpenAIModelOptions

RealtimePersonaplexModelOptions.description:
PersonaPlex (Cosmo Voice Light) model knobs — none tunable today; the
block exists so a PersonaPlex agent is representable.
RealtimePersonaplexModelOptions.title: RealtimePersonaplexModelOptions

RealtimePointAtObjectToolSpec.description:
Opt-in to the server-executed object locator, which returns points.

The sibling of ``detect_objects``: a marked point says one thing where
a box around a leaf includes everything behind it. Same zero-config and
availability terms.
RealtimePointAtObjectToolSpec.title: RealtimePointAtObjectToolSpec

RealtimeProviderCapabilities.description:
Which realtime model providers the caller may select per session.

Clients that surface a provider picker should hide it when
``openai_provider_available`` is false — a picker the server would
silently override is worse than no picker.
RealtimeProviderCapabilities.title: RealtimeProviderCapabilities

RealtimeReady.description: Sent after the upstream session is established and the agent is ready.
RealtimeReady.title: RealtimeReady

RealtimeReconnecting.description:
Server is transparently rotating the upstream session.

Emitted after the upstream signals an imminent shutdown when the server
has cached a resumption handle and is reopening the model session. The
transport and session state survive the swap; clients can show a brief
"reconnecting…" indicator and otherwise stay put.
RealtimeReconnecting.title: RealtimeReconnecting

RealtimeRejectedTool.description:
One tool spec the server refused, with the reason — so a client can
log *why* a spec was dropped instead of debugging silence.
RealtimeRejectedTool.title: RealtimeRejectedTool

RealtimeResolvedAgent.title: RealtimeResolvedAgent

RealtimeSay.description:
Idle-message action for a server hook: `text` = exact words,
`prompt` = model-generated per instruction, both unset = free model speech.
RealtimeSay.title: RealtimeSay

RealtimeScreenLocateToolSpec.description:
Opt-in to the server-executed screen locator.

Resolves a description to an element on the client's shared screen and
hands the model a ref addressing it, which the model passes to whichever
screen renderer the client declared (``cosmo_sdk_screen_click`` /
``cosmo_sdk_screen_highlight``). Not authorable: SDKs emit this entry
mechanically when the host supplies a screen-capture handler, whose
``screen_capture`` RPC the locator drives. Zero-config;
unknown fields are a schema error.

The locator itself has no availability gate. ``cosmo_sdk_screen_click``
does — clicking acts on the user's machine, so it stays behind the
desktop-control policy, and a session that cannot run it starts without
it and reports the drop on ``ready.rejected_tools`` under that name.
RealtimeScreenLocateToolSpec.title: RealtimeScreenLocateToolSpec

RealtimeServerEnvelope.description:
Generic chunked carrier for any oversized server message.

Mirror of ``RealtimeClientEnvelope`` for the server→client direction.
The server wraps any ``RealtimeServerMessage`` whose serialized JSON
exceeds the transport threshold into a sequence of these chunks; the SDK
buffers by ``envelope_id``, base64-decodes + concatenates, and
re-dispatches the inner message through the same handler path as
un-chunked messages.

``data`` is base64 over the UTF-8 bytes of the inner message JSON for
the same reason as the client side: keeps every chunk ASCII-safe so
byte-boundary splits never land mid-codepoint.
RealtimeServerEnvelope.title: RealtimeServerEnvelope

RealtimeServerToolSpec.description:
Opt-in to one server-executed tool by its dot-namespaced name
(e.g. ``"cosmo.web_search"``).

Deprecated: typed per-tool kinds (``web_search``, ``examine_image``,
``detect``, ``point``) supersede the generic name-reference, which is
honored only by the legacy ``/session/start`` flow and remains the only
path to ``cosmo.end_call`` / ``cosmo.view_state`` / ``cosmo.set_state``
until those gain typed kinds.

Server tools execute server-side; the session observes them through the
``tool-call`` / ``tool-dispatch-started`` / ``tool-result`` lifecycle.
Unknown names are rejected at session start with a typed 422
(``unknown_server_tool``).
RealtimeServerToolSpec.title: RealtimeServerToolSpec

RealtimeSessionConfig.description:
Session-start payload for external sessions — carried on the HTTP
session-start request (or as the first frame on the WS connect path).
The server replies with ``RealtimeReady`` once the agent is up.

Split into the two concerns of a session: ``agent`` (the persona — what the
model is) and ``session`` (per-run transport options). ``version`` enables
graceful version negotiation: the server can refuse with
``RealtimeError(code=version_mismatch)`` if the client speaks an
incompatible schema.
RealtimeSessionConfig.title: RealtimeSessionConfig

RealtimeSessionEnded.description:
The server ended the session on purpose. Published just before the
transport tears down so clients can render a clean terminal state
instead of treating the room drop as a failure. Delivery is
best-effort — the room close may still arrive first.
RealtimeSessionEnded.title: RealtimeSessionEnded

RealtimeSessionEndingSoon.description:
The server will end this session shortly (e.g. the max-duration cap
is about to fire). Clients may show a countdown; the session keeps
running until ``session-ended``.
RealtimeSessionEndingSoon.title: RealtimeSessionEndingSoon

RealtimeSessionParams.description:
Per-run, transport-level options for one session — continuity and other
knobs that vary run-to-run for the same agent. Audio config lives on the
``agent`` block (it's part of the agent, configured once).
RealtimeSessionParams.title: RealtimeSessionParams

RealtimeSessionResponse.description:
Public response shape for both cookie-auth and API-key session-start.

The two surfaces returned identical payloads; centralising the
model + the start-or-503 wrapper keeps them from drifting.

livekit_url.description: LiveKit room URL to connect to.
livekit_url.title: Livekit Url

RealtimeSessionResponse.title: RealtimeSessionResponse

RealtimeSessionStartTimings.description:
Server-side phase breakdown of session start (milliseconds).

Mirrors the ``starter_*`` fields of the "realtime session dispatched"
log line. Echoed to the client so it can emit one joined
startup-waterfall event (server + client phases) keyed by session_id,
instead of leaving the join to log archaeology.
RealtimeSessionStartTimings.title: RealtimeSessionStartTimings

RealtimeSilenceTimeout.description:
Server-runtime hook: perform `action` after `timeout_seconds` of user
silence.
RealtimeSilenceTimeout.title: RealtimeSilenceTimeout

RealtimeThinkingLevel.description:
Reasoning depth the client may request for the Gemini realtime model.

Mirrors ``google.genai.types.ThinkingLevel`` (minus the unspecified
sentinel). The server maps it onto the upstream enum; ``None`` on the init
leaves the per-participation-mode default in place.
RealtimeThinkingLevel.title: RealtimeThinkingLevel

RealtimeToolCall.description:
Model decided to invoke a server-executed tool.

Three-event lifecycle:
  ``tool-call`` (model decided)
    → ``tool-dispatch-started`` (server-side handler began)
    → ``tool-result`` (completed).
RealtimeToolCall.title: RealtimeToolCall

RealtimeToolDispatchStarted.description:
Server-side handler for the tool call began executing.

Sits between ``tool-call`` and ``tool-result`` to let UIs show a
"dispatching…" state — useful for slow tools where the gap between
model decision and result is multiple seconds.
RealtimeToolDispatchStarted.title: RealtimeToolDispatchStarted

RealtimeToolInvocation.description:
Server asks the connected client to run a tool locally.

Sent only for tools declared via ``kind="client"`` specs at session
start. The SDK runs the tool against the client's local resources and
returns the result out of band; the server validates it before
resolving the pending dispatch.

``request_id`` is the dispatch correlation id; ``tool_call_id`` is the
upstream's identifier for the underlying function call and is kept
distinct so observability messages (``tool-call`` / ``tool-result``)
still correlate by the upstream's id.

``origin`` identifies which producer authored the invocation:
``"realtime"`` for the voice model (default), ``"server"`` for a
server tool runtime reaching back through the same bridge. Clients
that don't render the distinction can ignore the field.

``executable`` is ``False`` for an informational mirror whose execution
runs out-of-band; ``True`` (default, and for a missing field) means the
recipient runs the tool.
RealtimeToolInvocation.title: RealtimeToolInvocation

RealtimeToolJobResult.description:
A long-running client tool finished off-band and is delivering its
terminal result. The server resolves the original tool call from
``job_id`` and injects the outcome; ``summary`` / ``error`` are the
model-facing text and ``result`` is structured data for logging.

Half of the background client-tool primitive — a tool whose work outlives
the RPC reply budget acks first and lands its outcome here. Every SDK
implements it, so it is protocol vocabulary rather than a first-party
extension.
RealtimeToolJobResult.title: RealtimeToolJobResult

RealtimeToolResult.description: Server-side tool finished. ``summary`` is a short human-readable line.
RealtimeToolResult.title: RealtimeToolResult

RealtimeTranscriptDelta.description:
Streaming transcript event for either speaker.

For the assistant role in audio sessions, this is the audio
transcription — the words the listener actually heard. The model may
ALSO emit a separate text channel via ``RealtimeModelText``; consumers
that render a "what was spoken" bubble should subscribe to
``transcript`` only.

Contract (wire-level, applies to both user and assistant):

* Streaming events (``is_final=False``): ``text`` is the **new
  fragment since the previous event** for that role's turn (a
  delta). Consumers append.
* Terminating event (``is_final=True``): ``text`` is the
  **cumulative full transcript** for the turn. Consumers replace
  whatever they accumulated with this value.

Two carve-outs where the terminating event is NOT the full turn, both
load-bearing rather than accidental:

* **Empty final.** A turn the model produced nothing usable for (a
  suppressed or garbled turn) finalizes with ``text=""``. It means an
  empty turn, not "unchanged" — a consumer that skips empty finals
  leaves the turn's bubble dangling into the next one.
* **Suffix final on a silent session.** When the agent runs with
  ``audio.output=False``, a user final that arrives after the VAD
  endpoint already committed the utterance is stripped of the committed
  prefix, so it carries only the remainder. Replacing on final would
  drop the part committed at the endpoint.

A consumer that only ever appends non-finals and replaces on final is
correct for the common path; these two need the extra handling.
RealtimeTranscriptDelta.title: RealtimeTranscriptDelta

RealtimeTtsProvider.description: External TTS providers Ultravox can render via ``externalVoice``.
RealtimeTtsProvider.title: RealtimeTtsProvider

RealtimeTtsVoice.description:
Provider-agnostic external-TTS voice selection. The runtime maps this to
the speech-to-speech provider's wire format (Ultravox ``externalVoice``
today). ``voice_id`` is the TTS provider's own voice id; the tuning fields
apply to ElevenLabs (Cartesia ignores the ElevenLabs-specific ones).
RealtimeTtsVoice.title: RealtimeTtsVoice

RealtimeTurnComplete.description: Marks the end of a turn so the client can finalize a transcript bubble.
RealtimeTurnComplete.title: RealtimeTurnComplete

RealtimeUltravoxModelOptions.description:
Ultravox model knobs. Valid only when the selected ``model`` runs on
Ultravox.
RealtimeUltravoxModelOptions.title: RealtimeUltravoxModelOptions

RealtimeUserSpeechTimeout.description:
A server-runtime silence timeout fired: the user was silent past a
configured threshold and the server performed `action`. Observability only.
RealtimeUserSpeechTimeout.title: RealtimeUserSpeechTimeout

RealtimeUserStartedSpeaking.description:
Server-side VAD detected user voice activity start.

Information-only — clients use this for UI indicators (mic-level
highlight, "listening…" label). Does NOT change client mic behavior;
the mic keeps streaming continuously so overlapping speech is captured.
RealtimeUserStartedSpeaking.title: RealtimeUserStartedSpeaking

RealtimeVerifyResponse.description:
Result of a credential preflight — a 200 means the credential
authenticated; the fields say what it can do from here.

can_start_sessions.description: Whether this credential carries the scope a session start needs. False means the credential is valid but under-scoped.
can_start_sessions.title: Can Start Sessions

external_user_id.description: The end user a minted token is bound to; null for an API key.
external_user_id.title: External User Id

realtime_voice_available.description: Whether this deployment has the default voice stack configured — LiveKit plus the default provider's key. A floor, not a per-session guarantee: a session that requests an opt-in provider is checked against that provider instead, so a start can still return 503 when this is true.
realtime_voice_available.title: Realtime Voice Available

scopes.description: Scopes granted to this credential, e.g. ``realtime:use``.
scopes.title: Scopes

workspace.description: The workspace the credential is bound to. Present for an API key, which the workspace's own developer holds; null for a minted token, which is held by an end user.

RealtimeVerifyResponse.title: RealtimeVerifyResponse

RealtimeVerifyWorkspace.description: The workspace the credential is bound to.
RealtimeVerifyWorkspace.title: RealtimeVerifyWorkspace

RealtimeVoiceConfig.description:
How the agent sounds: the prebuilt voice and the per-run speaking
style. One sub-object shared by both agent variants.
RealtimeVoiceConfig.title: RealtimeVoiceConfig

RealtimeWebSearchToolSpec.description:
Opt-in to the server-executed web-search tool, as its own typed kind.

The server owns the model-facing declaration (name, description, query
schema) — the client only opts in, so the spec carries no fields today.
Future configuration (result count, domain filters, freshness) lands as
typed fields here. Unknown fields are a schema error.

Typed per-tool kinds supersede the generic ``kind="server"``
name-reference, which is deprecated and not accepted by the
resolved-session flow. Availability is checked at session start: a
deployment or workspace that cannot run the tool starts the session
without it and reports the drop on ``ready.rejected_tools``.
RealtimeWebSearchToolSpec.title: RealtimeWebSearchToolSpec

TranscriptTurn-Input.description: One transcript line as written by ``RealtimeSessionLogger.log_transcript``.
TranscriptTurn-Input.title: TranscriptTurn

VoiceSession.description:
Developer-facing session record for the external (API-key) data-out
endpoints. Carries only product-agnostic fields — the workspace and the
end user are resolved from the credential, never echoed back.

Deliberately outside the ``Realtime*`` namespace: that prefix is swept
into the realtime wire-message codegen and the legacy spec, and this is a
REST response model, not a data-channel frame.
VoiceSession.title: VoiceSession

VoiceSessionImportRequest.description: Bundle for seeding a completed call: transcript + metadata + optional audio.
VoiceSessionImportRequest.title: VoiceSessionImportRequest

VoiceSessionTranscriptTurn.description: One transcript line as written by ``RealtimeSessionLogger.log_transcript``.
VoiceSessionTranscriptTurn.title: TranscriptTurn

ApiKeyAuth.description: Workspace-scoped API key. Pass as ``Authorization: Bearer <key>``. Required scopes are declared per-operation in ``x-required-scopes``.

info.description: Public CosmoRealtime API. Authenticate with a workspace-scoped API key carrying the ``realtime:use`` scope; the SDK handles LiveKit room join and the JSON control-plane wire protocol on top.
info.summary: Realtime voice and multimodal sessions over WebSockets and LiveKit.
info.title: CosmoRealtime API

post.description:
Mint a project-scoped JWT for one of the developer's end users.

The end user is provisioned as an external user that OWNS its project, so
every resource the resulting JWT creates attributes to the end user — not to
the developer (the API key owner, ``ctx.user_id``).

422.description: Rejected — see error.code (typed rejections) and error.errors (field-level validation)

post.description:
Start a session on the resolved-spec flow: the config is resolved
against the caller's workspace into a ``ResolvedSessionSpec`` and
dispatched; no ``RealtimeClientInit`` translation. A saved agent is
launched by reference (``agent: {type: "catalog", name}``) — resolution
stamps the session's agent linkage itself, so there is no out-of-band
attribution channel.

422.description: Rejected — see error.code (typed rejections) and error.errors (field-level validation)

post.summary: External Realtime Session Start Resolved Endpoint

422.description: Rejected — see error.code (typed rejections) and error.errors (field-level validation)

post.description:
Place an outbound phone call into a running realtime session.

The dialed party joins the session's LiveKit room as a SIP
participant and the agent — already in the room — converses with
them. Requires an API key carrying ``realtime:use`` plus the
workspace's phone-calls setting enabled, and is bound by its weekly
per-user minute limit. A minted end-user token is rejected (403
``dial_requires_api_key``); an unknown or ended session is rejected
(404 / 409).

get.description:
Report which realtime model providers the caller may select.

The Mac app hides its provider picker when the workspace is not
OpenAI-eligible — a picker the server would silently override is
worse than no picker. Declared before ``/{session_id}`` so the
literal path is matched ahead of the UUID path parameter.

post.description:
Import a recording bundle as a COMPLETED voice session (API-only).

Writes the transcript (and optional mono WAV) to the canonical GCS layout
and inserts a COMPLETED row, so the session reads back through the same
list/get/transcript endpoints and the recordings dashboard. Requires the
``recordings:write`` capability plus recordings-admin — the role that also
bridges ``realtime:use``, so the importer can read the session back (voice
reads are admin-only). Declared before ``/{session_id}`` so the literal
path wins over the UUID parameter.
